subject: Bayesian principal component analysis in STAN and JAGS using LOO as comparison

messages.author: 71c315ee557ff234
messages.subject: Bayesian principal component analysis in STAN and JAGS using LOO as comparison
parts:
Hi every,

motivation
the motivation was to run a bayesian PCA and compare the 
performance via the LOO Package with JAGS and STAN.
 
results
1. The good news is that STAN and JAGS performing similar considering the looic, et al. 
when using cholesky decomposition in STAN and wishart distribution in JAGS. 
2. The QR factorization of Ben to gain the eigenvalues/eigenvectors didn't performed well. 
The looic value doubled.
3. JAGS execution time is <1s, whereas STAN about order 20-30 times slower. 

sources
The JAGS/BUGS model based about code by Petr Keil.
http://www.petrkeil.com/?p=2316

can be downloaded directly from:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/petrkeil/bPCA/master/man/PCA.bugs

I didn't included it. 

I also did a variante using QR decomposition based upon the idea of Ben Goodrich
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/stan-users/JAD/stan-users/1-kJN4pu3vg/yyaaJF8kOAAJ

The JAGs parallel calling was inspired by Andrew Gelmann using the lecuyer module.

Questions
1. Can the PCA.stan be improved to match JAGS execution speed?
2. Did I make a mistake in coding PCA_qr.stan?

Thank you so much,
Andre

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Bayesian principal component analysis in STAN and JAGS using LOO as comparison
parts:
I looked at PCA Cholesky and it's about as good as you're going to
be able to code this in Stan.

We don't care about execution time---we care about n_eff/second (or
its inverse, second/n_eff) and to a lesser extent, convergence rate.
And you want to use Stan's posterior analysis, because it's much more
conservative about convergence than the techniques currently built into
JAGS/Coda.

Some of the issue is that if you have good conjugate priors and
the problem's not that hard, Gibbs can be really fast.

Also, those predictive computations in generated quantities are
going to kill you speed-wise, because each of those
multi_normal_log things requires factoring the matrix. We really
need to vectorize these. You should also be able to use the
multi_normal_cholesky() directly for the multi_normal_log calls.

- Bob

P.S. You don't seem to be using all your data in that program, but Stan's
OK with that.

messages.author: 8c4f70ab584cd6d9
messages.subject: Re: Bayesian principal component analysis in STAN and JAGS using LOO as comparison
parts:
Sorry for dredging this up, but I had been thinking about PCA recently.

I don't see the code above as performing any dimension reduction. It looks like just fitting a multivariate normal distribution, rather than PCA.

There was an earlier thread that looked at a probabilistic PCA approach last year. https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/stan-users/DYofzSAz1sk/iBlTEWcgGn8J

There were several suggestions to improve performance, though the OP did not post a followup whether they were successful. It would be interesting to see if their suggestions work. I was a little confused at how to integrate out the factors. For instance, most of the PPCA papers have the covariance matrix as something like WW'+I*sigma^2. Wouldn't the determinant of the covariance matrix be zero? The log determinant would then go to infinity, no?
